newsitem.title: TUNISIA: German Henkel in joint venture with Tunisian firm.
newsitem.headline: German Henkel in joint venture with Tunisian firm.

text.p: German chemical group Henkel Kga has signed with Tunisian firm Alki a joint venture for the development of detergent and cosmetic products manufacturing in the North African country.

Abdelhamid Bouricha, owner of Alki along with Abdelwahab Ben Ayed, told Reuters on Friday that Dusseldurf-based Henkel has agreed to take a 10 million dinars ($10 million) 51 percent stake in Alki's capital. The firm's name was changed to Henkel-Alki.
He said the contract has already been signed between the two parties and that the Tunisian government has given its agreement for the joint venture.
Bouricha said Henkel will contribute by its know how and technology to improve the quality of Alki's products and that the new firm aims at exporting to other Maghreb countries.
Alki has a plant in Mornag, southern Tunis and its detergents products were marketted under Nadhif brand. Its turnover was around 20 million dinars in 1996.
Bouricha owns with Ben Ayed Tunisia's leading privately-owned food industry group Poulina. ($=one dinar)
